records.rule: One multi-threaded XTP network service daemon per node takes registrations, service requests and peerages, and runs hooks (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-24).
xtpd has the linkage for firewall rule injection; peerages fill the nft set xtp_peers (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-24).
xtpd deals with lifecycle once, for every service on the node (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-24).
xtpd is where 'half the ship is gone, keep fire control up' sits (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-24).
On degrade xtpd drops to local emergency text files (Tom Dyer, 2026-11-24).
TCP and XTP opens are not one to one: an XTP address is a service name resolved to peers and routes; IP lives only in the route table.
The XTP open decides who, what, how urgent and which way in its first packet, before any state; bytes come last.
ooRexx decides (control plane); libxtp moves bytes (data plane); the data plane never waits on the control plane.
ssh.management is the first registration, with exec hook sshd -i; candidate 4 is replaced, not ported.
Every machine change goes to CODEX-PC marked NEEDS TOM'S DIRECT APPROVAL; orders never claim Tom approved.
Port 22 stays open on cats1 until SSH over XTP has survived a reboot.
Design only: nothing built or field-tested as of 2026-11-24.
